title: 1986 AHSME Problem 2
statement: If the line \(L\) in the \(xy\)-plane has half the slope and twice the \(y\)-intercept of the line \(y=\frac23x+4,\) then an equation for \(L\) is

solutions.text:
The original line has slope \(\frac{2}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \(4.\) Therefore \(L\) has slope \(\frac{1}{3}\) and \(y\)-intercept \(8,\) so its equation is \(y=\frac13x+8.\)

Thus the correct answer is A.
hints: Read the slope and intercept from \(y=mx+b\)
Apply the two requested changes to the coefficient and constant separately
